segments.dry: A couple of reviewers with dry or slightly dry skin report smoother, plumper, more bouncy-feeling skin after a month or so of use; one notes that on very dry mornings the serum alone isn't rich enough without a moisturizer layered on top.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin, including one who describes it as 'ridiculous sensitive,' report the serum is gentle, hydrating and did not irritate or break them out.
segments.mature: Reviewers with mature, perimenopausal or postmenopausal skin, including one buying it for her 75-year-old mother, report firmer, more elastic, tighter-looking skin and visibly softer fine lines after weeks to a couple of months of consistent use.

concerns.aging: Reviewers targeting fine lines, elasticity and firmness report visible plumping, firming and softened fine lines, generally after several weeks to two months of consistent use; reviewers note it works gradually rather than overnight and is not a miracle product.
concerns.dehydration: Reviewers report smoother, softer, well-hydrated skin after regular use; one reviewer notes the serum alone isn't rich enough on very dry mornings and needs a moisturizer layered on top.
concerns.blemishes: Material is limited to two reviewers with sensitive skin who report the serum never caused irritation or breakouts for them.

While I like to look put together and occasionally go all out with hair and make up, I’m really a low maintenance kind of lady. The high cost of products and learning the proper way to use products has always been a turn off for me, so I’ve never had a skincare routine. However dry wrinkled aging skin is a bigger turn off! Now, at age 45 and perimenopause setting in, aging has begun. I decided about 8 months ago it was long past due that I started a skin care routine and try to preserve any healthy youth I have left in my skin. After lots of research I decided to try the brand Ordinary. The main driving point of selecting this brand was cost. After 8 months of trying several items in their product line, here is my take away. Pros Affordability being number one.: Highly budget-friendly, allowing a full, effective, science-backed full skincare routine to be built for under $100 Transparency: Clear, ingredient-focused formulas (e.g., Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1%, Hyaluronic Acid 2% + B5) with no hidden additives. Effectiveness: I definitely see an improvement in my skins texture, hydration, and brightness. Range: Wide variety of products addressing specific concerns, including acne, aging, and hyperpigmentation. Cons Complexity: It is confusing when trying to build a routine; It requires research to understand layering, contraindications, and proper application. Ive been using the line for almost a year and I still feel like I go at it blind and should be doing more or doing things

extraits.titre: Surprisingly, I’m seeing small results with this!Surprisingly, I’m seeing small results with this!
extraits.texte: For every 10 skin care products that I hear about and purchase, I usually see real results on about .25 of them. I’m a sucker for an instagram influencer and have bottles of serums i’ve purchased to attack my menopausal skin. However, I am actually pleasantly surprised with the serum. I’m not sure if it has something to do with this brand’s hyaluronic serum, but I’ve heard that theirs supposedly goes deeper than surface level. I’m not sure what peptides do, but I am seeing little results after about half of a bottle, and about two months. I put this on at night after washing my face. I put some moisturizer on top of it. I wouldn’t say that this is a miracle worker, and no one else has noticed a difference in my skin, but I feel like my elasticity is better and there are less fine lines, probably because my skin is more plump. I do like this brand because I feel like you get more for the money and I’ve been pleased with everything I’ve tried.

extraits.titre: Happy with the results at a really good price
extraits.texte: For the cost this stuff works really well. I'd been using the Drunk Elephant polypeptide cream for years (which I also found effective!) but got my first facial recently and the facial artist (what are they called? lol) said a serum is better so now I use both. After ~2 months there is a noticeable difference in the feel of my skin. It is like... bouncy. I'm 37 years old. I always felt this way after putting on the Drunk Elephant cream but now I wake up with super soft skin before applying anything. It's much smoother. I recently added the Ordinary's "Hyaluronic Acid 2% + B5 (with Ceramides)" and am not sure how much more it's doing, but I was already seeing positive results from this serum after just a month or so. Some people on here complain about the price and I'm curious where you might get something else effective, ethical, and decent quality for this price because I think $19 is pretty good for a bottle that lasts me 2 months and has results like these! For context, I'm a 37-year-old female with slightly dry skin and use this twice a day.

This has become one of my favorite skincare items! Goes on very lightweight and doesn’t feel sticky or anything. Very hydrating and layers well under makeup. Doesn’t break me out and I have somewhat sensitive skin, so it’s a very gentle product.

I’ve repurchased this serum several times and it has become a regular part of my skincare routine. I mainly use it for the combination of peptides and hyaluronic acid, as I want something that supports hydration while also targeting fine lines, firmness and overall skin texture. The formula contains several different peptide technologies as well as amino acids and multiple forms of hyaluronic acid, which is a good combination for the price. The serum itself does leave a noticeably sticky layer on my skin rather than absorbing to a completely dry finish. I find that I need to use a fairly lightweight moisturiser over it, as richer products can sometimes pill. That is not a major issue for me because I have experienced the same thing with quite a few serums, and once I know which products layer well with it, it is easy enough to work around. With regular use, my skin feels well hydrated and smooth, and I like having a peptide serum as part of my routine for the longer-term benefits to the appearance of fine lines and elasticity. A few drops are enough for my whole face, so a bottle lasts a reasonably long time. I also keep coming back to this particular one because the price on Amazon is competitive and I feel the formula offers good value compared with many other peptide serums. Despite the slightly sticky finish, it works well for me and I have been happy enough with the results to keep repurchasing it.
I bought it for my mom, she's 75 years old and she loved it, because after the first use her skin tightened and she looked more youthful. It's a good size and can be used twice a day
